`src/Encina.MongoDB/Sagas/SagaStoreMongoDB.cs:129-132`: `GetStuckSagasAsync`'s filter (`Filter.Eq(s => s.CompletedAtUtc, null)` + `Filter.Lt(s => s.LastUpdatedAtUtc, threshold)`) has no status filter at all, unlike the other 9 providers' `WHERE (Status = 'Running' OR Status = 'Compensating') AND LastUpdatedAtUtc < @ThresholdUtc` (e.g. `src/Encina.ADO.SqlServer/Sagas/SagaStoreADO.cs:158-159`) and unlike Mongo's own `GetExpiredSagasAsync` two methods below in the same file (`SagaStoreMongoDB.cs:154-158`), which correctly reuses the `ActiveSagaStatuses` (`Running`, `Compensating`) filter. `TimeoutAsync` (`SagaOrchestrator.cs:447`) sets `Status = TimedOut` without setting `CompletedAtUtc`, so on MongoDB a timed-out saga is incorrectly and *permanently* re-surfaced by `GetStuckSagasAsync` forever (its `CompletedAtUtc` never becomes non-null), while on the other 9 providers it is correctly excluded from "stuck" once its status leaves `Running`/`Compensating`. (Note: a `TimedOut` saga cannot also appear in the "expired" batch on MongoDB — `GetExpiredSagasAsync`'s own status filter, `SagaStoreMongoDB.cs:155`, restricts results to `Running`/`Compensating` and excludes `TimedOut` by construction; the two batches are mutually exclusive on this point, the defect is the stuck-batch misclassification alone, not a double-appearance.) Fails AGENTS.md §5 provider coherence ("providers share the same interfaces... and differ only in implementation").
